title: Who Gets the Desk? A Simulated Case Study of Unequal Access in Two School Districts · 原句词汇
instructions: 按确切源词形、词义与原句完成三写三读及三轮测试。已学词与新词分别安排，不把重复复制当作跨天掌握。

vocabulary.sourceQuote: Southfield, near the industrial port, has one overcrowded primary school and a waiting list of 240 children.

passage:
overcrowded — 过于拥挤的
Southfield, near the industrial port, has one overcrowded primary school and a waiting list of 240 children.

attendance — 出勤率
The council’s own data showed that Southfield’s attendance rate was 87%, compared with 96% in Northbank.

barrier — 障碍
The report did not say that transport was the only cause of absence, but it listed transport as a “major barrier.” This gap in the plan showed how budgets can shape which problems are addressed first.

voluntary — 自愿的
“If they spend time in Southfield, who will teach our children?” The council replied that tutoring would be voluntary and would happen after school hours, so Northbank pupils would not lose lessons.

donated — 捐赠
Second, it would provide 120 used laptops to Southfield, donated by local companies.

average — 平均的；平均数
Last September, the city council published a report showing that Southfield’s classrooms held an average of 38 pupils, while Northbank’s held 22.

condition — 条件
The council accepted the offer, but with a condition: the minibus would run only on weekdays and only for children in years 1 to 6.

review — 审查；复核
The council said it would review the situation in December, leaving older students and their families in an uncertain position for most of the year.
